title: Burst mesh consolidator and deviation ledger for smoother dedicated fleet scaling
author: Nikhil Rao
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets experience short, high-amplitude microbursts that cause repeated oscillation in autoscaler decisions and noisy utilization metrics. This PR introduces a burst mesh consolidator component and a deviation ledger to reduce sensitivity to ephemeral spikes while preserving throughput guarantees for latency-critical tenants. Summary of changes: 1) Add a burst mesh consolidator that aggregates per-tenant transient demand signals across pool boundaries and emits smoothed surge tokens to the autoscaler; 2) Introduce a deviation ledger that tracks signed deviations between observed utilization and committed throughput at multiple percentiles, enabling proportional soft-reservations and controlled preemption windows; 3) Add a stability window heuristic and probabilistic dampening so small bursts are consolidated into warmlet reservations rather than triggering full provision ramps; 4) Wire consolidated signals into the existing provisioner/vacuum path with a compatibility shim to fall back to legacy behavior when feature flag is off; 5) Instrument telemetry and dashboards with new HDR sketches and delta counters for auditability and SLO reconstructions. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: docs/design/burst_mesh_consolidator.md - [x] Unit tests for consolidator and deviation ledger - [x] E2E burst simulation job - [x] Dashboard and alert updates - [x] Feature-flagged rollout. Rollout plan: start gated rollout to internal Dedicated fleets with feature flag off by default, enable in Canary pool for 48h, evaluate SLO regressions and util stability, then widen to 20% then full. Backout strategy: immediate feature flag flip and reconcile reservations via ledger reversal if anomalous provisioning is detected. Context and related work: builds on prior warm-pool and headroom work (ENG-2148, ENG-2710) and addresses issues surfaced during incident RED-2025. This PR focuses on the control-plane signal handling and lateral aggregation, not on kernel-level serving changes, keeping serving runtime untouched. Why different: instead of hard quota bumping, the consolidator creates transient soft-reservations and issues conserved surge tokens; the deviation ledger provides a compact, auditable trail of what was reserved, granted, and reclaimed, enabling later chargeback and post-mortem reconstruction.

review_comments: Ava Martinez: Can the consolidator produce false positives when many small tenants burst in phase? Please add a guardband to avoid unnecessary warmlet allocation.

Nikhil Rao (reply): Added a stability window and probabilistic dampening to the mesh so that correlated microbursts only cause warmlet reservations until sustained demand persists. See mesh_consolidator.go:stabilityWindow()
Marta Kovacs: The deviation ledger persistence format needs a migration note for clusters that upgrade mid-surge. Please ensure ledger ticks are idempotent across restarts.

Nikhil Rao (reply): Ledger write is idempotent by design and includes a monotonic tick. Added migration tests and notes in docs/design. Also added reconciliation method ledger.Reconcile() to handle partial writes.
Ethan Li: CI flaked on e2e burst sim in one run, can you add retry and a shorter fixture to speed up runs?
Nikhil Rao (reply): Added backoff/retry and shortened default sim to 5m for CI. Full 30m sim runs as nightly job.
release_notes: Introduce burst mesh consolidator and deviation ledger. Improves autoscaler stability during microbursts by consolidating transient demand into warmlet reservations and providing an auditable deviation trail. Feature-flagged rollout. No breaking changes to serving runtime.
